Interface GridModel

All Known Implementing Classes:
AbstractGridModel, ComputedGridModel, ListGridModel, PagedGridModel, TreeGridModel
public interface GridModel

The data shown by a Grid: a rectangle of values addressed by row and column. The grid asks only for the cells it shows, so the values can come from anywhere: a list of objects (ListGridModel), a function (ComputedGridModel), a database cursor, or objects laid out as columns. Rows and columns can both have names, and each cell may hold a value of any type.

The grid reads the model on the JavaFX application thread, so data must only change there and events must be fired there. AbstractGridModel.applyChange(Runnable) takes care of this for changes from other threads.

    • sortRows

      default boolean sortRows(List<SortKey> keys, IntFunction<Comparator<Object>> order)
      Sorts the rows at the source, for models that do it better than the grid, such as a database query. If it returns true, the model has reordered its rows and fired an event, and the grid does not sort itself (it clears the selection instead of following the rows). The default returns false: the grid sorts.
      Parameters:
      keys - the columns to sort by, the first one decides and the next ones break its ties; empty for the model's natural order
      order - the order of a model column's values, ascending, nulls first: the column's comparator or the grid's default order (numbers by value, text ignoring case). Models that sort somewhere else, such as in a database, can ignore it.
      Returns:
      true if the model sorted its rows
